anchor: Returns a single value; no representation of uncertainty about the missing values.
Uncertainty obtainable only by wrapping the method in external resampling (e.g. bootstrap, MC-dropout, ensembles); no native pooling rule.
Natively produces multiple stochastic draws, but no established pooling rule or evidence of near-nominal interval coverage.
Multiple draws with an established pooling rule (e.g. Rubin's rules); near-nominal coverage shown in published simulations under MAR.
Level 4 and recommended as the uncertainty-propagating approach in clinical methods or reporting guidance.
Opaque learned model; no component of the imputation rule can be inspected.
Partially inspectable learned structure (attention maps, explicit observation graph), but no per-variable model.
Non-parametric but inspectable (variable importance, donor neighbours, out-of-bag error per variable).
Explicit per-variable conditional models whose form and coefficients can be printed and checked, with standard diagnostics.
Rule stated fully in one sentence; no fitted model.
Biased unless data are MCAR.
Valid under MAR (correct model); no MNAR mechanism, sensitivity parameter, or use of missingness pattern.
Valid under MAR and either supports a standard MNAR sensitivity analysis OR uses the missingness mask/indicators as model input.
A published member explicitly models the MNAR mechanism (selection, pattern-mixture or self-masking) under stated identifying assumptions.
Level 4 and validated on clinical data within an established sensitivity-analysis framework.
Known to distort subgroup distributions (e.g. shrinkage to a global value) or to drop subgroups differentially; no audit mechanism.
No built-in subgroup handling; subgroup error audit possible only post hoc, without per-value uncertainty.
Can condition explicitly on subgroup variables/interactions and supports post-hoc subgroup error audit.
Level 3 and uncertainty allows subgroup-level interval reporting, with clinical evidence that subgroup-aware imputation reduces disparity.
Explicit fairness constraint or objective built into the imputation, validated on clinical data.
Deep model needing GPU, extensive tuning and large training sets for clinical-scale data.
Deep or graph model trainable on CPU for small/medium data; tuning required.
Iterative fitting repeated m times or tree ensembles; minutes on 10^4-10^5 rows on CPU.
One fitted model per variable; seconds on 10^4-10^5 rows on CPU.
Closed-form or no fitting.
No reference implementation or documentation standard.
Reference implementation exists; reproducible with seeds and stored weights, but no standard diagnostics.
Seed-reproducible open-source implementation with some standard diagnostics (e.g. OOB error).
Established software with documented diagnostics, and covered by reporting-guideline items.
Level 4 and named as an accepted primary or sensitivity procedure in regulatory/trial guidance.
